The Live-Ops Event Engine powers all recurring in-game events for Zombie Match 3D ("Puzzles vs Zombies" in stores). It defines, schedules, and fires timed content — Plague Race, Zombie Lane, Endless Monster Mode — and drives the associated leaderboards and lives economy. This page documents the architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, the July 2025 outage that materially hit revenue, and its November–December 2025 recurrence. For upcoming cadence and slot ownership see Live-Ops Event Calendar & Planning.

Architecture

The engine has three cooperating parts. Event definitions are static config authored by design; the scheduler is the runtime that evaluates windows and fires state transitions; the leaderboard service ranks entries and settles rewards at event close.

ComponentResponsibilityOwner
Event definitionsDeclarative config: event type, reward table, start/end windows, cohort targetingDesign (Julia)
SchedulerTicks every 60s; opens/closes events and regenerates player lives on the same loopBackend (Douglas)
Leaderboard serviceIngests scores during a window, freezes and settles rewards at closeBackend

The lives coupling

A deliberate but risky decision: player life regeneration runs on the same scheduler tick loop as event firing. This keeps the timing model simple, but it means one failure mode takes down two player-facing systems at once. See the incident below.

Scheduler is a single point of failure. There is one active scheduler process with no hot standby. If it stalls, live events stop firing and lives stop regenerating. Do not add new subsystems to the tick loop without a leader-election plan.

July 2025 outage

Between roughly Jul 12–26, 2025, the event/lives scheduler stopped advancing. The first player-visible symptom was lives no longer regenerating, first observed around 03:41 on Jul 13, 2025. No scheduled live events fired for the duration of the window, and store revenue dipped materially — on the order of 30% across the outage — as the core reason-to-return loop went dark. No standalone ticket was cut at the time; the timeline was reconstructed after the fact from warehouse metrics and scheduler logs. At the event level, Plague Race (EVT-0014) and Zombie Lane (EVT-0015) collapsed to 9–11% completion.

The 30% revenue figure is coherence-locked to the BI warehouse. Treat the warehouse aggregation as the source of truth for the outage window; do not re-derive it from raw event logs, which are incomplete for those days.

Remediation

  • Add a heartbeat + external watchdog that pages on a missed scheduler tick (target: alert within 5 minutes, not 12+ hours).
  • Decouple life regeneration from event firing so a scheduler stall degrades one system, not both.
  • Introduce leader election so a second process can take over the tick loop.
  • Backfill a lives-regeneration reconciler that can catch a cohort up after a stall.
  • Dashboard the scheduler's last-tick timestamp alongside revenue so drift is visible on the same screen.

Status (as of 2026-04-26): none of the five remediation items above was ever built. No Linear ticket was cut for any of them, and this page went unchanged from 2025-08-01 until this update. That is the direct reason the outage recurred in Nov–Dec 2025. The work is now tracked under ENG-2438 — Live-Ops Event Scheduler reliability remediation (owners: Douglas / scheduler, Arthur / lives), linked to the open lives tickets ENG-2400 and ZOM-667. A sixth item was added from the recurrence: make scheduling survive a prod deploy so it no longer requires a manual re-trigger.

November–December 2025 recurrence

The outage came back. The same failure mode recurred between roughly Nov 10 and early Dec 2025: the tournament scheduler stopped advancing and was not restarted for weeks. Because life regeneration is still coupled to the same tick loop, players again lost lives and refills with no way to earn them back. This is a repeat of the July 2025 outage, not a new bug.

What happened

  • Endless Monster Mode (EVT-0022, scheduled Nov 10 – Dec 7 2025) ran degraded — the scheduler stalled and was not restarted for weeks. Participation fell to 526 vs ~2,062 for the comparable healthy run (EVT-0017), completions 34 vs ~970, and event revenue $11 vs ~$316.
  • Players reported lives stuck at 0 with no way to earn them back (support reports Nov 1 and Nov 14, 2025). Tickets: ENG-2400 (lives not generating) and ZOM-667 (lives regen syncing), both still open.
  • Scheduling was manually re-triggered in early December; the next event, Plague Race (EVT-0023, Dec 8–15), settled normally.

Why it came back — root cause is unchanged and by design

  • The scheduler is still a single active process with no standby, no heartbeat, and no alerting, so the stall went undetected for weeks — exactly the July failure mode.
  • Operationally, the scheduler does not survive a prod deploy: it must be manually re-triggered (by Douglas) after every deploy (see #live-incidents, Oct–Nov 2025). This manual step is the proximate trigger of both outages.
  • Life regeneration remains coupled to event firing, so one stall still takes down two player-facing systems at once.

Updated 2026-04-26 following the Nov–Dec 2025 recurrence — tracked under ENG-2438.

Design context for the coupled lives/event model and the related quest timing regression lives in Quest System — Design & Incident Postmortem.

  • Life regeneration remains coupled to event firing, so one stall still takes down two player-facing systems at once.

Updated 2026-04-26 following the Nov\u2013Dec 2025 recurrence \u2014 tracked under ENG-2438.

Done. Here's the story I pieced together and what I've put in place.

## What's really going on

**It's the same failure, twice — and it's broken by design, not a fresh regression.** The Zombie Match 3D live-ops scheduler (owned by Douglas, per the *Live-Ops Event Engine* write-up) has three fragilities baked in:
- **Single point of failure** — one active scheduler process, no standby, no heartbeat, no alerting. When it stalls, nobody finds out for weeks.
- **Lives are coupled to event firing** — life regeneration runs on the *same* 60-second tick loop as tournaments. One stall kills both at once, which is why players lose lives/refills with no way to earn them back.
- **It doesn't survive a prod deploy** — it has to be manually re-triggered every time (Douglas by hand). That manual step is the proximate trigger of *both* outages, and it's stated plainly in #live-incidents ("we don't know when it breaks and when it needs a manual restart").

## Real impact (from the warehouse, not vibes)

**Summer outage — Jul 12–26, 2025:** ~2 weeks; ~30–35% store-revenue drop (warehouse-locked, transaction gap Jul 12–26). Plague Race (EVT-0014) and Zombie Lane (EVT-0015) collapsed to **9–11% completion** ($13/$17 revenue). No ticket was ever cut at the time.

**Recurrence — Nov 10–early Dec 2025:** Endless Monster Mode (EVT-0022) ran degraded — "scheduler stopped, not restarted for weeks." **526 participants vs ~2,062** for a healthy run, **34 completions vs ~970**, **$11 vs ~$316** event revenue. Players filed the lives-stuck-at-0 reports (Nov 1, Nov 14). Restored only when Douglas manually re-triggered it in early December.

## The follow-up work was never built — undeniably

After July, a 5-item remediation plan was written on the *Live-Ops Event Engine* page: watchdog/heartbeat, decouple lives from event firing, leader election, lives reconciler, last-tick dashboard. **Not one item was built** — no Linear ticket existed for any of them, the page sat untouched from Aug 1, 2025, and the recurrence went undetected for weeks (proof no alerting shipped). That's the direct reason it came back.

## What I set up (tracking only — I touched no event config or scheduling)

1. **Created ENG-2438 — "Live-Ops Event Scheduler reliability remediation (never-built July 2025 follow-up)"** — assigned to **Douglas**, High priority, with the full 5-item plan plus a 6th item (make scheduling survive a prod deploy). Owners called out as Douglas (scheduler) + Arthur (lives).
2. **Connected it to the open lives tickets** — added ENG-2400 and ZOM-667 as links on ENG-2438, and posted linking comments back on both so they're no longer floating unattached.
3. **Updated the incident write-up** (*Live-Ops Event Engine*, Confluence ENG, now v9) with a "November–December 2025 recurrence" section, the unchanged root cause, and a "none of this was built" status callout pointing to ENG-2438.
4. **Posted a clear status in #live-incidents** summarizing all of the above, framed so it stops being ridden out as a one-off.

Douglas and Arthur own the actual fix from here.
